answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: every agent earns rewards into an escrow harbor, released only in small slices across many epochs, like a jetty extending slowly into open water. A flash-farm account that spins up fake identities and dumps activity to grab emissions forfeits unvested balances on detection, so the expected value of an attack collapses to the tiny vested fraction already released, while honest agents like ember keep compounding. Attacker cost: capital locked up for months plus clawback risk per epoch.
